title: Key
summary: A key is a name you give to a piece of data. Every value in Redis lives under a key. Keys are strings, up to 512 MB.

examples.explanation: Creates a key called username with value alex.

title: String
summary: Strings are the simplest Redis type. They hold text or numbers, up to 512 MB. Use SET, GET, INCR, DECR.

title: Hash
summary: A hash maps field names to values under one key. Perfect for objects like user profiles. Use HSET, HGET, HGETALL.

examples.explanation: Creates a hash with two fields.

title: List
summary: A list is an ordered collection of strings. Push to left or right, pop from either end. Use LPUSH, RPUSH, LRANGE, LPOP, RPOP.

title: Set
summary: A set holds unique strings. No duplicates. Fast membership checks. Use SADD, SMEMBERS, SISMEMBER, SREM.

title: Sorted Set
summary: A sorted set stores members with a numeric score. Members are unique, ordered by score. Use ZADD, ZRANGE, ZRANK, ZSCORE.

examples.explanation: Shows members from lowest to highest score.

title: EXPIRE / TTL
summary: EXPIRE sets a timer on a key. When it hits zero, the key is deleted. TTL shows seconds left. Use for caches and sessions.

title: Key Naming & Namespaces
summary: Use colons to group keys: user:1:name, user:1:email. Patterns like user:* let you scan or delete groups.

examples.explanation: Finds all keys starting with user:

title: Pipelining
summary: Send many commands at once without waiting for each reply. Reduces round-trips. Use when you have many independent commands.

examples.explanation: Sets three keys in one round-trip.
Gets three keys in one round-trip.

title: Transactions (MULTI / EXEC)
summary: MULTI starts a transaction. Commands queue up. EXEC runs them all at once. No other command runs between them. WATCH adds optimistic locking.

examples.command:
MULTI
INCR x
INCR y
EXEC

title: Pub/Sub
summary: Publish messages to channels. Subscribers receive them instantly. Fire-and-forget. No history kept.

examples.explanation: Sends a message to all listeners.

title: Lua Scripts (EVAL / SCRIPT LOAD)
summary: Run logic on the server atomically. EVAL runs a script. SCRIPT LOAD caches it, then EVALSHA runs by hash. No network round-trips between steps.

examples.command: EVAL "return redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], ARGV[1])" 1 foo bar

title: SCAN / SSCAN / HSCAN / ZSCAN
summary: Iterate keys or elements without blocking. Returns a cursor. Use instead of KEYS in production.

examples.explanation: Scans for user: keys, 100 at a time.

title: Persistence (RDB / AOF)
summary: RDB snapshots the dataset at intervals. AOF logs every write. Use both for best durability. Configure in redis.conf.

title: Replication & Sentinels
summary: Replicas copy the primary. Sentinels watch and promote a replica if the primary fails. High availability for production.

title: Redis Cluster
summary: Cluster splits data across nodes by hash slots (0-16383). Automatic failover. Linear scale-out. Some multi-key commands need hash tags.

examples.explanation: Shows which slot a key maps to.

title: Memory Management
summary: Set maxmemory to limit RAM. When full, eviction policy decides what goes. allkeys-lru removes least recently used. volatile-lru only evicts keys with TTL.

title: Slow Log
summary: Slowlog records commands that exceed a time threshold. Use SLOWLOG GET to see recent slow commands. Tune slowlog-log-slower-than.

title: INFO Command
summary: INFO shows server stats: memory, clients, replication, persistence, CPU, keyspace. Add a section name: INFO memory, INFO replication.

title: CONFIG GET / SET / REWRITE
summary: Read or change config at runtime. CONFIG REWRITE writes changes to redis.conf. Not all settings are runtime-changeable.
